pages.x: On the morning of 11 September 2001, 19 men of al-Qaeda, a terrorist group led by Osama bin Laden, hijacked four airliners soon after they took off from airports in the eastern United States. Some had trained as pilots in America. Armed with knives and box cutters, they took the controls, to turn planes full of fuel into weapons.

At 8:46 the first plane hit the North Tower of the World Trade Center in New York, and at 9:03 the second hit the South Tower, as millions watched on live television. People trapped above the fires waved from the windows. Within two hours both towers, 110 storeys tall, had collapsed in clouds of dust, killing thousands, among them 343 firefighters.

At 9:37 a third plane hit the Pentagon, the headquarters of the US military, near Washington. On the fourth, United 93, passengers and crew learned by phone what had happened to the others, and fought back. The plane crashed into a field in Pennsylvania, short of its target in Washington. All 40 passengers and crew died.

The dead were office workers and cleaners, passengers, firefighters and police, and they came from more than 90 countries. Thousands of the people who worked for months in the dust at Ground Zero later fell ill, and many have since died.
pages.of: people killed in a single morning

pages.x: President George W. Bush declared a war on terror. NATO, for the first and only time, invoked its rule that an attack on one member is an attack on all. When the Taliban, who ruled Afghanistan, refused to hand over bin Laden, America and its allies attacked them in October 2001.

Airports brought in strict security checks. The United States opened a prison for terror suspects at Guantánamo Bay, and new laws let the government watch people more closely. Muslims in the West faced suspicion and attacks. Within two years America was at war in Iraq too.

September 11 was the deadliest terrorist attack in history. It drew the United States into wars in Afghanistan and Iraq that lasted twenty years. Bin Laden was found and killed in Pakistan in 2011. Where the towers stood, two pools now fill their footprints, with the names of the dead cut around them.
pts: Four planes were hijacked on 11 September 2001
It led to the war in Afghanistan
